summary: A type whose copies equal their original and change independently of it, so values can be copied, assigned and compared like integers.
definition: A type whose copy, assignment and equality behave as they do for `int`: a copy compares equal to its original, and changing one never affects the other. Sparkles requires it of events and identifiers so tests can compare and replay them; see [local reasoning](/research/sean-parent/local-reasoning).

authority.text: Sean Parent: contracts and regular types

summary: A design in which a protocol or state machine performs no I/O itself: the caller supplies bytes, time and events, and performs the actions it returns.
definition: A protocol or state-machine implementation that never reads, writes, sleeps or consults a clock. Its caller feeds it input and carries out the effects it requests, which makes the core deterministic and testable without sockets or timers. [Writing Specification Docs](/guidelines/spec-docs) asks for this separation wherever the domain permits.

summary: The decision whether a candidate matches a fuzzy query at all, made separately from how highly it ranks.
definition: In `sparkles:fuzzy`, a query part admits a candidate when the part, after deleting at most its typo budget of characters, occurs in order within the candidate. Admission alone decides which candidates match and what is highlighted; ranking only orders the admitted ones.

summary: The one deterministically chosen set of candidate characters that proves a fuzzy match and is highlighted to the user.
definition: Of all the ways an admitted query part can be found in a candidate, the one with the fewest deleted query characters, then the earliest final character, then the earliest positions. It supplies both the highlighted ranges and the window the ranking score is computed over.

summary: One font inside a font file: the whole file for a single-font file, or one member of a collection, identified by the file's bytes and an index.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, one font inside a byte buffer, read in place and never changed after it opens. A single-font file holds one face; an [OpenType collection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/otff#font-collections) holds several, picked by index.

summary: A face at a particular size, with one fixed set of variable-font coordinates and any faked styling, from which every glyph, metric and shaping result is derived.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, a copyable value combining a [face](/glossary#face), a size in pixels per em, one vector of [normalized variation coordinates](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/otvaroverview#coordinate-scales-and-normalization) and a [synthesis](/glossary#synthesis). It is the only place variation coordinates are stored, so shaping, metrics, outlines and rasterization all read the same ones. Not to be confused with an OpenType *named* instance.

summary: What font matching had to fake to approximate a requested style: an emboldening amount, a slant, or a variation-axis setting.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, the value a match returns alongside the chosen face, saying how to approximate what the face lacks: embolden by an amount, skew by an angle, or set an axis. Shaping and rasterization both consume it, so faked bold and italic look the same everywhere.

summary: The fixed box a terminal lays characters out in, with its baseline, underline and strikeout positions, in whole device pixels.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, the cell width and height, baseline, and underline and strikeout positions and thicknesses derived from a face at a size, rounded to whole device pixels by one documented rule. The cell width is the advance of the digit zero.

summary: A value that fully determines one rendered glyph, so equal keys always produce identical pixels and caches can be keyed by it.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, the face identity, glyph, size, variation coordinates, subpixel offset and render flags of one rasterization. Equal keys produce byte-identical output, which is what makes glyph caches separate values instead of state inside a face.

summary: Somewhere fonts come from: explicit files, a directory, the bundled fonts, or the system's list of installed fonts.
definition: An input to the [font catalog](/glossary#font-catalog): explicit files, a directory, the font directory Sparkles bundles, or the files the platform lists as installed. A platform source only lists files; the library's own parser describes them.

summary: What the font catalog stores about one face: enough to match it and to test which characters it covers without opening it.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, the catalog's description of one [face](/glossary#face): names, style, width, weight, spacing and character coverage, read by the library's own parser and cached on disk against the file's size and modification time.

summary: The index of known fonts built from every font source, over which matching and fallback run identically on every platform.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, the set of [face records](/glossary#face-record) built from all [font sources](/glossary#font-source). Platforms differ only in which files they list; matching and fallback rules over the catalog are the same everywhere. Distinct from a collection index, which picks a face inside one file.

summary: The ordered list of fonts consulted, character by character, when the preferred font cannot draw a character.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, an ordered list of [face records](/glossary#face-record) beginning with the matched face and keeping only faces that add character coverage. A face opens on first use, and each character's answer is remembered.

summary: Used alone, the fraction of each pixel a glyph's shape covers, which a rasterizer produces; which characters a font maps is called character coverage.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, the 8-bit per-pixel value a rasterizer writes for a glyph: 0 where the outline leaves the pixel empty, 255 where it covers it. The set of characters a face maps through its `cmap` table is called *character coverage*.

summary: A rendered sample of a font: preview text, a waterfall of sizes, a code sample, a glyph map or a comparison, shown as one image.
definition: In the font explorer, a block of sample text or glyphs rendered in the font being examined. Every specimen is one bitmap the font library rasterizes, shown as an image in a window or over the kitty graphics protocol in a terminal, never drawn in the terminal's own font.

summary: One of three layouts the font explorer chooses from its width in interface cells: wide, medium or narrow.
definition: In the font explorer, the layout chosen by width measured in interface cells, so one rule serves a window and a terminal: *wide* at 150 cells or more shows every pane, *medium* folds the sources into the family list, and *narrow* below 100 shows only the specimens with the other panes as overlays.

summary: A check that lists every glyph whose width differs from a terminal cell and every ligature that changes the number of glyphs.
definition: In the font explorer, the check that tells whether a programming font keeps a terminal's character grid: glyphs whose advance differs from the face's [cell metrics](/glossary#cell-metrics), and ligatures that change the glyph count, each with the characters involved.
